title: The grapes
subtitle: Grüner and Riesling
objectives: Describe Grüner Veltliner in the Wachau

steps.title: Grüner Veltliner
steps.body: Grüner Veltliner, Austria's signature grape, covers over half the Wachau. It grows best on deeper loess soils on lower slopes, giving full, peppery wines with citrus, green apple, white pepper and, in riper styles, stone fruit and spice. Its pepper comes from rotundone.

steps.title: Riesling
steps.body: Riesling covers about 20%, but makes many of the most prized wines. It's planted on the steepest, stoniest terraces of gneiss and granite, where Grüner would struggle. Wachau Riesling is dry, powerful and mineral, with peach, apricot and citrus. Famous vineyards include Achleiten, Kellerberg, Loibenberg and Singerriedel.

steps.prompt: Match each grape to its soil.
steps.explanation: Grape follows soil in the Wachau.

steps.body: Wachau Riesling and Grüner from the same producer and vintage make a great side-by-side tasting of grape and soil.

steps.prompt: Where is Riesling planted in the Wachau?

steps.title: What you learned
points: Grüner Veltliner covers over half, on loess
Riesling grows on steep rock terraces
Both are made dry and powerful
